thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: prometheus_scrape_errors_high (prod-metrics) + log_ingest_lag_high (prod-logs) — triggered by 3m window. pd.incident/1978887777 links: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/1978887777. Runbook: https://confluence.example/runbooks/prom-scrape-log-lag

maria: acked. I'm oncall — taking triage. Adding context: two alerts fired together, looks correlated. Starting runbook step 1 (check exporter pods + scrape latency).

jamie: grafana: https://grafana.example/d/metrics/cluster-overview?var-job=metrics-exporter — exporter pods in prod-eu zone CPU ~95-99%, avg scrape latency jumped to 8-12s for several targets. Prom errors are 5xx from exporter endpoints.

maria: noted. I see a recent deploy of service x that enabled detailed debug metrics (high-cardinality). That would explain scrape time ballooning. Plan: 1) bounce exporter pods in affected AZ to shed long-lived connections 2) push temporary relabel_config to drop debug metrics until we revert the app flag.

kevin: +1 for relabel. Quick relabel snippet:```yaml
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__name__]
    regex: 'debug_.*'
    action: drop
```Apply via k8s configmap in prometheus-prod (will take ~30s to roll).

anya: on logs side: logstore-ingester consumer group lag >1.2M (kafka topic prod-logs), ES bulk_rejections spiking (~450/s). Kibana shows "es_rejected_execution_exception" and GC pressure on es-data-2. Seems like indexing storm from a new feature that increases event size.

liam: customers impacted? Support: ingestion for analytics pipelines delayed, search/observability ingest roughly 20-60m delayed depending on backlog. No direct API request failures for customer-facing latency right now. Recommend we mark customer impact as degraded ingestion (major).

maria: agreed. Status: P1 degraded ingestion, not full outage. Posting short status to status.redwood.example: "Ingestion delays for analytics/logs in prod — working on mitigation; no API downtime detected."

jamie: mitigation plan for logs: 1) scale logstore-ingester replicas from 5->12 to consume backlog 2) decrease ES bulk size temporarily (from 5MB -> 1MB) 3) remove/rollback new feature flag in service-y that's causing large events. I'll run the k8s scale now:```bash
kubectl -n prod-scale deploy/logstore-ingester --replicas=12
```ETA ~2m for pods to be ready.

kevin: scaling ES data nodes would help too but requires longer lead time. I'll open an infra job to add +2 nodes if backlog persists after consumers scale.

anya: I've applied a temporary consumer throttling tweak to slow write pressure: adjusted bulk_size in ingester config and restarted a single ingester pod as canary. Watching rejections.

maria: done with prometheus relabel config push, restarting prometheus server in prod-eu to pick up config. Expect scrape failures to drop in ~30-60s. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by maria (oncall). Autoscroll: next escalation in 12m if not resolved.

jamie: metrics errors dropped 90% after relabel + exporter bounce. CPU on exporters falling to ~40%. Scrape latency back to normal range. Grafana link: https://grafana.example/d/targets/prom-scrape-targets

anya: ES rejections dropped to ~80/s after ingester scale and bulk size change, kafka lag trending down from 1.2M -> 600k in 10m. Continuing to monitor.

liam: customer comms: posted to the internal incidents slack and flagged for support on priority. Support to send proactive note to top 5 customers with big pipeline usage.

maria: handing off to kevin as next oncall at 1978887850. Key follow-ups for next oncall: - confirm kafka lag continues down to <50k - if not, trigger ES scale + investigate larger rollback of feature flag - runpostmortem checklist and capture offending metric names to prevent future scrapes.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll keep the incident open for 2 hours and then switch to postmortem. Thanks team. :wave:

maria: thanks all, nice triage and fast mitigations. Filed a short followup ticket: https://jira.example/browse/RI-4321 — include metric names and owner action items.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident resolved by kevin (ack cleared) at 1978887875.
